text.arabic_uthmani: وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصَٰرِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُوا۟ ٱلذِّكْرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُۥ لَمَجْنُونٌۭ

words.gloss_range: opening connective with resumptive, boundary-linking, and live-backdrop force
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens as a boundary connector, not padding. It carries the movement from the prior prophet narrative into a fresh report of live hostility, so the present threat is heard as part of the same controlled discourse rather than an isolated insult. The clipped opening also lets the assertion arrive quickly, but that sound detail serves the larger pivot.

topics.headline: resumptive boundary pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah turning from the prior prophet scene into a present Prophet-facing threat without severing the discourse link.
topics.reason: The opening connector is licensed as a discourse boundary marker by its position before the main near-harm clause.

topics.headline: circumstantial live backdrop
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hostility can be heard as an ongoing circumstance around the addressed Prophet, not only a later sequel.
topics.reason: The circumstantial reading is compatible with the main threat report and preserves the live setting of the clause.

topics.headline: clipped connective onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the quick pickup before the emphatic opening, which makes the report begin with compressed urgency.
topics.reason: The short particle immediately precedes the assertion frame, giving the onset a real but secondary cadence payoff.

words.gloss_range: lightened assertion particle whose force is resolved by the later distinguishing lām, not a local conditional
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:ʾin}}) sets the report in assertion mode before the hostile actors are named. The later lām resolves the particle as lightened emphasis rather than a conditional, so the near-harm is not framed as a hypothetical. This outer assertion also anticipates the accusers' own emphatic quote near the end of the ayah.

topics.headline: lightened assertion resolved by later lām
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the threat is asserted as real near-harm, not suspended as an if-clause.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as lightened emphatic with a possible conditional alternative, and the later distinguishing lām resolves the local parse toward assertion.

topics.headline: outer scope over the full threat report
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the assertion frame covers the multi-beat report, including trigger and quoted response.
topics.reason: The particle occurs before the main near-action clause and scopes over the report into which temporal and speech clauses are embedded.

topics.headline: outer frame anticipates inner accusation frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices two assertion frames bracketing the ayah: the narration asserts the threat, while the opponents assert their accusation.
topics.reason: The opening lightened assertion with lām is structurally mirrored by the later full assertion plus predicate lām inside the quote.

words.gloss_range: ongoing near-completion auxiliary: hostility presses toward realized harm while remaining uncompleted
words.root_gloss_range: root range centers on nearing or almost doing; local unnegated imperfect selects near-completion rather than scarce occurrence
words.prose: {{ar:يَكَادُ}} ({{tr:yakādu}}) makes the hostility a sustained threshold. The disbelievers press toward an action, but the auxiliary keeps the harm at near-completion rather than accomplishment. Its complement is the causative threat that follows, so the ayah first names an almost-breach, then explains its visual channel, its hearing trigger, and the repeated saying that carries the same pressure into speech.

topics.headline: ongoing near-completion without completion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a real hostile pressure held at the edge of accomplishment rather than a completed injury or harmless intention.
topics.reason: The unnegated imperfect auxiliary carries live near-completion; local grammar gives no negation that would reverse the force toward scarcely.

topics.headline: auxiliary governs the causative harm verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word does not stand alone; it controls the following caused-slipping action as the approached but uncompleted event.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following causative verb the predicate governed by the near-completion auxiliary.

topics.headline: near-harm tied to perception and speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the near-threshold verb belongs to the ayah's larger sensory and speech pressure field, including visual danger and repeated saying.
topics.reason: The supplied rows connect near-completion with perceptual threat, including sensory danger scenes such as 2:20 and the ocular-warning comparison at 12:67, without making those passages control the local parse.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural relative that makes the hostile subject a known collective defined by the following denial clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) names the hostile side as a definite plural class whose identity is completed by the following denial clause. The relative pronoun holds the subject open until denial arrives, then the same collective continues through hearing, gazing, and saying.

topics.headline: known group defined by denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the actors are not anonymous opponents; they are grammatically identified by completed denial.
topics.reason: The definite relative head requires the following relative clause, so the hostile subject is completed by the denial predicate.

topics.headline: plural relative sustains collective agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices one plural collective moving through the ayah's hostile actions rather than separate unrelated agents.
topics.reason: The masculine plural relative agrees with the plural verbs and pronouns that carry the same group through the clause chain.

words.gloss_range: completed Form I denial defining the group before its present hostile response; covering/denial pressure remains locally ironic against sight
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes covering, ingratitude, and denial; local Form I perfect selects established denial while preserving covering irony
words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) completes the subject by settled denial before any present attack unfolds. The Form I perfect makes denial the group's defining act, while the covering sense of the root sharpens the irony: those who cover over the Reminder use sight as their weapon. The later speech accusation becomes the outward voice of that established denial.

topics.headline: completed denial defines the subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that hostility proceeds from a settled identity of denial, not from a tentative disagreement.
topics.reason: The perfect Form I verb forms the relative clause predicate and carries the plural subject internally, defining the relative group before the threat predicate begins.

topics.headline: covering irony against weaponized sight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that those marked by covering-denial weaponize perception against the Reminder.
topics.reason: The local sense remains theological denial, while the root's covering field survives as irony because the ayah immediately makes their gazes the instrument of harm.

topics.headline: denial recurs as hostile response to Reminder
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that denial is not static here; it becomes hostile perception and quoted speech after the Reminder is heard.
topics.reason: The supplied co-occurrence and same-surah rows link denial with Reminder rejection and speech, while the local syntax specializes the pattern in this gaze-and-quote scene.

words.gloss_range: distinguishing and emphatic lām attached to the threatened causative action
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) is the lām that locks the earlier particle into assertion and places emphasis directly on the threatened causative verb. The ayah asserts the reality of the near-harm while the near-completion verb still keeps the harm from being completed. This first lām also starts a frame answered by the later emphatic lām before the accusation.

topics.headline: lām distinguishes assertion from condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the report is grammatically secured as assertion rather than conditional possibility.
topics.reason: QAC identifies this as the distinguishing lām following lightened assertion, and its attachment to the verb resolves the earlier particle.

topics.headline: emphasis lands on the harm action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that emphasis falls where the destabilizing action is named, not only on the auxiliary.
topics.reason: The lām is fused to the causative complement verb, so the assertion targets the approached action within the near-completion frame.

topics.headline: first lām in the ayah-wide assertion frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a double-lām architecture: one asserts the narrated threat and the other the opponents' quoted certainty.
topics.reason: The first lām at word 6 is structurally answered by the emphatic lām at word 16.

words.gloss_range: Form IV causative near-harm directed at the addressee: make-slip, destabilize, or eye-strike through hostile gaze
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes slipping, smooth ground, and destabilization; the local Form IV plus gaze instrument selects caused slipping or ocular harm
words.prose: {{ar:يُزْلِقُونَكَ}} ({{tr:yuzliqūnaka}}) is the ayah's densest threat word: a Form IV causative aimed at the second-person object. It pictures hostile gazes trying to make the addressed Prophet lose footing, with the eye-strike construction making the gaze more than passive looking. The accepted Form I variant is useful as contrast, because it highlights how the canonical local form foregrounds mediated causation. Its rarity makes this ocular destabilization a marked lexical choice, and its sliding sound texture suits a slip that ends in impact.

topics.headline: Form IV causative with direct second-person object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Prophet is grammatically bound into the verb as the direct affected target of a caused destabilization.
topics.reason: The local Form IV imperfect with object suffix supplies causative force and a direct patient.

topics.headline: slippery-ground image becomes ocular harm
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the concrete loss-of-footing image transferred into hostile gaze, not merely a generic attempt to harm.
topics.reason: Dictionary evidence supports slipping and eye-strike language, and the local instrumental gaze phrase licenses the ocular application.

topics.headline: accepted variant clarifies causative force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the variant comparison makes the canonical Form IV causation more visible, while the variant does not replace the local surface.
topics.reason: The variant is valid contrast evidence, but the aligned local word remains Form IV and therefore keeps mediated causation as the selected analysis.

topics.headline: verb gathers the first attack beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this verb as the anchor that gathers subject, object, instrument, and timing into one hostile scene.
topics.reason: The attachment graph makes this verb the predicate of the near-action clause with object suffix, instrumental complement, and temporal clause.

topics.headline: near-hapax causative destabilization
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the text chooses marked vocabulary for this ocular destabilization rather than an ordinary harm verb.
topics.reason: The contextual profile marks the local form as low occurrence, supporting lexical salience without expanding the meaning beyond the local construction.

topics.headline: sliding consonant texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a secondary sound-shape that fits the slipping image without carrying the lexical analysis by itself.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation is locally tied to the threat word and remains secondary to the causative and lexical evidence.

words.gloss_range: instrumental-causal preposition making the gazes the mediated means and trigger of the attempted harm
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) makes the gazes the mediated channel of the action. The preposition keeps the eyes from becoming the direct object; they are the means, and in context also the cause, of the near-slipping. Because it follows the object suffix, the target is heard before the instrument is revealed.

topics.headline: gazes as means and cause of harm
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the attack works through their gazes as an instrument and trigger, not through physical contact.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the gaze noun as complement to the causative verb, licensing instrumental and causal readings.

topics.headline: preposition blocks direct-object reading
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the gazes are not what is made to slip; they explain how the Prophet is targeted.
topics.reason: The direct object is the suffix on the verb, while the gaze noun is governed by the preposition.

topics.headline: postposed fused instrument phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sequence: affected target first, weapon phrase second, timing trigger third.
topics.reason: The preposition fuses to the gaze noun and follows the object-bearing verb before the temporal clause begins.

words.gloss_range: possessed plural gazes or perceptual faculties used as the instrument of hostile destabilization
words.root_gloss_range: root range spans sight, seeing, perception, and insight; local plural possessed noun selects gazes/perceptual faculties as instrument
words.prose: {{ar:أَبْصَٰرِهِمْ}} ({{tr:abṣārihim}}) names not a neutral act of seeing but the hostile collective's owned gazes as instrument. The plural and suffix multiply the force and route it back to the deniers. Because the root field can include insight as well as sight, the ayah inverts perception: hearing the Reminder produces weaponized seeing rather than recognition. That weaponized gaze also reverses the humbled-eyes scene within the surah (68:43), and the sharp sound of the phrase fits its role as a pointed instrument.

topics.headline: owned plural gazes as governed instrument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the instrument is plural, possessed, and tied back to the hostile group.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the preposition and carries a possessive suffix referring to the same plural subject.

topics.headline: perception and insight inverted into harm
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a field normally capable of perception or insight is turned into hostile scrutiny.
topics.reason: The local noun selects gazes or perceptual faculties, while broader insight language survives as moral inversion rather than a separate active sense.

topics.headline: hearing triggers weaponized seeing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sensory architecture: the Reminder is heard, and sight becomes the assault medium.
topics.reason: The local sequence places the gaze phrase before the temporal hearing clause, while the temporal clause explains what activates the attack.

topics.headline: hostile eyes against humbled eyes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a same-surah reversal between weaponized eyes here and humbled eyes at 68:43.
topics.reason: The supplied rows explicitly contrast 68:51 with 68:43, supporting a local surah-level gaze reversal.

topics.headline: sharp perceptual cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a secondary pointed cadence in the gaze phrase that fits its role as instrument.
topics.reason: The sound observation is tied to the local surface and remains secondary to the instrumental grammar.

words.gloss_range: temporal-causal hinge: when, and in context because, they heard the Reminder
words.prose: {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) is the hinge where the ayah turns from the attack mechanism to its trigger. It marks the moment of hearing and, in context, the cause of the hostile reaction, so the same compact clause can explain both the gaze assault and the speech accusation. A root-rarity claim does not add much here because the local evidence treats the word as an adverbial particle rather than a lexical root item.

topics.headline: when-because trigger of hostility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that hearing the Reminder is both the time when the hostility erupts and the trigger that explains it.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the temporal clause an adverbial setting for the near-harm, and coordination lets it explain the subsequent saying as well.

topics.headline: root-rarity claim without local payoff
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The local particle function already carries the meaningful payoff; the root-rarity count does not change the reading of this word.
topics.reason: QAC aligns the word as a temporal adverbial particle with no lexical root assignment, so the root-count claim adds no separate reader-facing payoff here.

words.gloss_range: completed reception of the Reminder by the same hostile collective, with hearing as meaningful input but not obedient heeding
words.root_gloss_range: root range spans hearing, listening, understanding, and heeding; local response blocks obedient heeding while preserving meaningful reception
words.prose: {{ar:سَمِعُوا۟}} ({{tr:samiʿū}}) gives the hostile group a completed reception event. They have heard the Reminder, and the root's range can include understanding, but the context blocks obedient heeding because their response is gaze attack and accusation. The word is therefore the hinge from received message to hostile counter-speech, with a minor nasal sound thread carrying the hearing beat toward the closing label.

topics.headline: same collective completed the hearing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same deniers who were defined earlier are now the hearers whose reception triggers the response.
topics.reason: The perfect plural verb has an implicit subject recovered from the hostile collective.

topics.headline: meaningful hearing without heeding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reaction is to meaningful received discourse, while obedience or compliant heeding is blocked by the hostile context.
topics.reason: The root can extend toward understanding or heeding, but the local response narrows it to received hearing without obedient uptake.

topics.headline: hearing links sight and speech responses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what they hear becomes both hostile seeing and hostile saying.
topics.reason: The supplied rows connect hearing with the Reminder, sight, and saying; local syntax makes the Reminder the direct object and the trigger clause the hinge.

topics.headline: sound thread toward the final label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a minor acoustic binding between the hearing beat and the closing accusation.
topics.reason: The sound row adds a small cadence payoff that remains subordinate to the trigger grammar.

words.gloss_range: the known Reminder as the direct heard object, a preserved and active message that triggers both attacks
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes remembering, reminding, mention, and preserved record; local definite gerund/title selects the known Reminder
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلذِّكْرَ}} ({{tr:al-dhikra}}) is the known Reminder as the direct object of hearing. Its semantic field is not inert text: it carries reminding, mention, and preserved memory, which is exactly what denial resists. Structurally it sits between gaze and speech, and the next ayah expands the same root beyond the hostile hearers to the worlds.

topics.headline: definite direct object of hearing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hostile reaction is directed at a known received message, not an undefined sound.
topics.reason: The definite accusative noun is the direct object of the hearing verb and immediately precedes the coordinated saying clause.

topics.headline: reminder, mention, and preserved record
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the attacked object functions as active reminder and preserved mention, not merely as a neutral title.
topics.reason: The local word remains the definite Reminder, while the broader remembering and preserved-record field survives as semantic pressure.

topics.headline: pivot between gaze and accusation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the Reminder as the structural center: it explains the gaze behind it and provokes the saying after it.
topics.reason: The object of hearing stands between the attack mechanism and the coordinated speech clause, and supplied rows connect the title with denial and saying.

topics.headline: next-ayah widening beyond hostile hearers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word provoking hostility in 68:51 is immediately widened beyond them in 68:52.
topics.reason: The supplied rows connect this title with Quranic self-designation and preservation references (15:9, 38:1), and with the immediate recurrence at 68:52.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector adding the speech assault to the gaze assault while keeping the two modes distinct
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the verbal assault to the visual one. It opens a new finite clause after the heard object, so the final saying is not an apposition to the Reminder but a coordinated hostile response. The connector keeps gaze and speech distinct while making them cumulative.

topics.headline: speech assault coordinated with gaze assault
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah pairs silent visual aggression with public verbal accusation.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the saying clause with the hostile action clause, preserving two distinct but linked attacks.

topics.headline: new finite clause after the heard object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the turn from the hearing trigger into the quote beat rather than a continuation of the object phrase.
topics.reason: The conjunction is fused to the speech verb and begins the coordinated finite clause.

words.gloss_range: ongoing active saying that turns denial into repeated public accusation
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers saying, utterance, opinion, and asserted stance; local imperfect speech verb selects repeated public accusation
words.prose: {{ar:يَقُولُونَ}} ({{tr:yaqūlūna}}) makes the accusation an ongoing active speech habit. The same plural deniers who heard and gazed now speak, and their saying governs an embedded emphatic quote. The word turns private hostility into public classification, with the madness label functioning as a repeated dismissal formula rather than a neutral report; within the surah, verdict speech also marks failure at 68:26.

topics.headline: speech verb governs the emphatic quote
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusation is quoted with its own internal assertion grammar, not merely summarized.
topics.reason: The speech verb governs the quoted complement formed by the later assertion particle, predicate lām, and accusation noun.

topics.headline: imperfect active plural keeps accusers exposed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices repeated accusation by visible agents, not an anonymous passive report.
topics.reason: The imperfect active plural verb keeps the speakers recoverable as the same hostile collective.

topics.headline: speech performs hostile classification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the saying tries to make the label socially operative as the speech-output of denial.
topics.reason: The root can include uttered stance, and the local quote turns denial after hearing the Reminder into a public label.

topics.headline: surah verdict speech and dismissal formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final saying belongs to a wider verdict-speech pattern in the surah (68:26) and to a prophetic dismissal formula.
topics.reason: The supplied rows compare verdict speech at 68:26 and connect the saying-madness pairing to repeated prophetic dismissal, while the sound row binds the speech verb to the final label.

words.gloss_range: emphatic quote opener with fused pronoun; the local referent is the addressed Prophet, while message-target resonance is secondary
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:ʾinnahu}}) lets the accusers' rhetoric expose itself from inside the quote. The particle and pronoun fuse assertion with the target, setting up a topic-comment accusation completed by the final predicate. Some rows press a Prophet-or-message ambiguity, but the local cross-reference evidence strongly routes the pronoun to the same addressed Prophet; the message remains involved by context, not as an equal grammatical antecedent. The inner assertion also answers the ayah's opening assertion frame and reintroduces the madness charge already denied at 68:2.

topics.headline: fused emphatic topic-comment frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the accusers staging their claim as formal certainty inside the quote.
topics.reason: The particle governs the pronoun as its noun and prepares the predicate reinforced by the later lām.

topics.headline: pronoun routing targets the Prophet locally
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusation grammatically targets the addressed Prophet, while the Reminder is implicated by the hearing context.
topics.reason: The supplied CRITICAL ambiguity is narrowed because cross-reference evidence strongly licenses the pronoun as referring to the same masculine singular addressee targeted earlier.

topics.headline: opening assertion answered by quoted assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an assertion-frame echo: divine narration opens the threat, and the accusers close with their own emphatic claim against the denial already stated at 68:2.
topics.reason: The lightened opening assertion and the full quote assertion form a structural echo, and the same madness-root accusation recalls the opening negation at 68:2.

words.gloss_range: predicate-focused emphatic lām binding certainty directly to the closing accusation label
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) concentrates the accusers' certainty on the predicate label. It does not add a new idea; it binds emphasis directly to the accusation that closes the ayah. As the second lām, it answers the earlier lām of the threat and turns their own overassertion into part of the ayah's exposed rhetoric.

topics.headline: emphasis fused to the accusation predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that certainty is concentrated on the closing label, making the accusation a verdict rather than a passing noun.
topics.reason: The lām precedes the predicate of the quoted assertion and is fused to the accusation word.

topics.headline: second lām completes the two-lām frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah framed by two emphatic lāms: one asserting near-harm, the other asserting hostile diagnosis.
topics.reason: The lām at word 16 parallels the lām at word 6, creating an assertion architecture across narration and quote.

words.gloss_range: indefinite passive-participle accusation: a classifying label of one supposedly acted upon or veiled, with broader concealment-root pressure narrowed to rhetoric
words.root_gloss_range: root range links concealment, hidden beings, covered places, shields, embryos, gardens, and madness; local passive participle selects the accusation label while broader concealment pressure remains rhetorically live
words.prose: {{ar:مَجْنُونٌۭ}} ({{tr:majnūnun}}) is the final quoted label, an indefinite passive participle rather than an event verb or abstract noun. The accusers classify the Prophet as a type, as one supposedly acted upon or veiled. The broader concealment root family remains rhetorically live, but locally it is narrowed to the accusation: hiddenness is weaponized as a charge. The word also returns the surah to the madness charge denied at 68:2, now placed in the opponents' mouth, and the same dismissal formula appears in other prophetic opposition scenes (15:6, 26:27, 44:14, 51:39, 52:29). Its heavy nasal close remains a sound payoff, while the local grammar carries the accusation.

topics.headline: indefinite predicate classifies as a type
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quote assigns the Prophet to a category rather than reporting a specific episode.
topics.reason: The indefinite nominative predicate completes the quoted assertion as a classifying label.

topics.headline: passive participle makes the target acted upon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusation grammatically portrays the accused as acted upon, not as an active claimant.
topics.reason: The local form is a passive participle, not a finite verb or abstract madness noun.

topics.headline: concealment family weaponized as insult
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the intended insult draws on a wider concealment family, while the local word remains the madness or possession accusation.
topics.reason: The broad root field includes hiddenness and garden-related concealment, but local grammar selects the passive-participle accusation, so the broader family survives as narrowed rhetorical pressure.

topics.headline: repeated prophetic madness-dismissal formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the label belongs to a recurring opposition formula (15:6, 26:27, 44:14, 51:39, 52:29), not a one-off insult.
topics.reason: The supplied references identify the accusation formula across prophetic opposition scenes (15:6, 26:27, 44:14, 51:39, 52:29), while 68:51 specializes it as the terminal verbal assault.

topics.headline: opening denial returns as closing quoted assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the surah-level reversal: what was denied of the Prophet at 68:2 is reasserted by opponents near the close.
topics.reason: The same accusation family appears in the opening denial at 68:2 and returns here as hostile quoted assertion.

topics.headline: nasal closing sound intensifies the label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the heavy nasal close as a sound payoff, while the phonetics do not by themselves prove the possession imagery.
topics.reason: The nasal cadence is real on the surface, but the stronger claim that sound enacts possession is narrowed to acoustic heaviness.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction يَكَادُ ... لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصَارِهِمْ joins near-completion, causative slipping, and the eyes as instrument.
baseline_models.mechanism: A hostile gaze acts like loss of traction: it applies enough pressure to approach bodily or social displacement, while يَكَادُ holds the result at a threshold rather than reporting completion.

activation_trace.role: The nearly-doing image supplies the threshold that keeps the attempted displacement just short of completion.
The slippery surface on which a foot cannot hold supplies the mechanics of induced loss of position.
Literal ocular seeing identifies the eyes as the channel through which the destabilizing pressure is applied.

changed_reading.before: They look at the addressee with extreme hostility.
changed_reading.after: Their looking is an almost-effective operation of traction loss that tries to remove the addressee from a bodily, social, or discursive position.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The temporal sequence لَمَّا سَمِعُوا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَيَقُولُونَ makes hearing the reminder the input and the madness claim the output.
baseline_models.mechanism: Audible reception fails to become understanding or compliance. The reminder is instead rerouted through public speech into a diagnosis that represents the speaker's cognition as veiled.

activation_trace.role: Hearing sound supplies the literal sensory input that immediately precedes the hostile response.
Hearing as understanding and compliance supplies the unrealized receptive outcome against which their reaction is measured.
The reminder or admonition image makes what is heard a cognition-addressing prompt rather than undifferentiated sound.
Circulating public talk turns the spoken madness label into a repeatable social verdict rather than a private thought.
Madness as a veil over the mind supplies the content of the diagnosis produced by the failed reception.

changed_reading.before: They hear the reminder and then utter an insult.
changed_reading.after: The ayah maps a failed reception pipeline: sound enters, understanding is refused, and the reminder is converted into a circulating diagnosis of its bearer.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ and لَمَجْنُونٌ place two covering images on opposite sides of an intervening act of sight.
baseline_models.mechanism: Those characterized by covering or rejecting truth use their own visual judgment to claim that another person's mind is covered. The accusation therefore mirrors, and may externalize, the obscuration named in the agents.

activation_trace.role: Concrete covering supplies the obscuring action associated with the agents.
Covering or rejecting truth locates the agents' obscuration specifically in their response to what is presented as true.
Inner sight and certainty make their gaze an implicit claim to epistemic penetration, not only ocular force.
The veiled-mind image returns covering as the predicate they assign to the addressee.

changed_reading.before: Disbelievers correctly see a person and falsely call him mad.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages rival claims about hidden cognition: agents marked by covering deploy sight to project a second covering onto the mind they oppose.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The split mapping of يَكَادُ permits a non-dominant ك ي د shadow alongside the dominant near-action construction, while gaze and speech form two coordinated channels.

changed_reading.after: 'He is mad' is also an unwarranted adjudication: the opponents claim power to define a person's mind while the context strips their judgment of text, guarantor, and demonstrated truth.

context_deltas.mechanism: A vertical reversal joins the scenes. In the focus, their eyes are instruments meant to cast another off balance; in the preceding scene, those same possessed eyes are lowered while abasement overtakes their owners. The direction of ocular force rebounds.

context_deltas.mechanism: The nearby counterfactual trajectory runs from constricted containment toward being cast into exposed space, but catching grace interrupts it and selection reverses casting-away into drawing-near. strongest_changes: The focus became a failed reception mechanism in which hearing does not become understanding and sight does not become insight, so both senses are redirected into diagnosis and attack.
The attempted slip became reversive: lowered hostile eyes, the garden excluders' deprivation, and gradual counter-displacement all turn force back toward its agents.
The nearby catch-cast-exposure-selection sequence changed near-slipping from a narrow miss into an intercepted expulsion trajectory.
The requested mutual oiling unexpectedly activated a material model in which accommodation smooths away traction and enables one-sided displacement.
summary.what_was_special: The trace was driven by cross-domain branch contacts that a single paraphrase would erase: written line versus slippery surface, social oiling versus traction loss, ocular height versus lowered eyes, and casting-out versus selection. Split-root shadows preserved coordinated stratagem and speech-as-instability without displacing the dominant readings.
remaining_uncertainties: The force of بِأَبْصَارِهِمْ can remain bodily, affective, reputational, or analogically terrain-changing; the packet does not force one domain.
The ك و د to ك ي د and ق و ل to ق ل ل split activations are productive but must remain secondary to the dominant mappings.
The oiling/slipping and stone-ground/slippery-ground links may be deliberate material mechanisms or only branch-enabled resonances.
The context strongly supports reversal and interception, but it does not uniquely specify what prevents the focus displacement from completing.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A gaze used to remove footing.** `ك و د B002` supplies nearing an act, `ك ف ر B003` rejecting truth, `ز ل ق B001` sliding from place, and `ب ص ر B001` sight. The instrumental *bi-abṣārihim* assigns the eyes an aggressive role. I infer hostile visual pressure -> destabilized footing; the ayah turns looking into attempted displacement while preserving that the act nearly, rather than fully, succeeds.
2. **Surface smoothing returns as social attack.** `ز ل ق B007` supplies oiling and polishing until smooth, activated by the reciprocal oil/compromise image `د ه ن B001/B002` in 68:9. I infer when conciliatory smoothing fails, the same surface logic becomes an attempt to make the addressee slip. The later ayah retrospectively sharpens 68:9: compromise and hostile gaze are different tactics serving one desired loss of firmness.
3. **Hearing without compliance produces accusation.** `س م ع B001` supplies hearing, while `س م ع B003` supplies understanding and compliance; `ذ ك ر B009/B003` supplies reminder and bringing to mind; `ق و ل B001` supplies utterance; and `ج ن ن B006` madness veiling mind. The temporal *lammā* makes accusation follow reception of the reminder. I infer sound reaches the ear but is blocked from obedient understanding, so the hearers relocate disorder into the messenger's mind. The ayah exposes the charge as a failed-hearing response.
4. **Reminder, reputation, and circulating speech.** `ذ ك ر B004/B007` supplies mention and honorable renown, while `س م ع B005` supplies public circulation and `ق و ل B007` circulating talk. I infer the reminder's public reach provokes a rival reputation campaign, “madman.” The ayah therefore stages conflict not only over content but over which mention will circulate.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 68:52 immediately and exclusively reclassifies what they heard as *dhikr*, not evidence of madness. Its universal destination also outscales their local reputation attack: the mention they try to control is directed beyond their circle.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Hostile sight tries to turn standing into slippery ground.** Fixed `لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ` activates `ز ل ق B001` (sliding from place and smooth barren ground), while fixed `أَبْصَارِهِم` activates `ب ص ر B001` (seeing and the seeing organ). Open exposure in 68:49 and firm reintegration in 68:50 supply vulnerable surface and restored position; I infer that concentrated looks function socially to remove footing and dislodge the addressee from that standing. The gaze is an attempted spatial operation, not passive observation.
2. **Sound enters the ear but does not become compliant understanding.** Fixed `سَمِعُوا` activates `س م ع B001` (hearing sounds) and the unfulfilled `س م ع B003` (understanding and compliance). Their immediate fixed `يَقُولُونَ` activates `ق و ل B013` (held doctrine), and fixed `مَجْنُون` activates `ج ن ن B006` (mind-veiling madness). The packet supplies hearing followed by a preexisting interpretive label; I infer that doctrine blocks the arrow sound → understanding and substitutes accusation. The ayah diagnoses reception failure after successful audition.
3. **The reminder's public honor is attacked by a covering label.** Fixed `ٱلذِّكْر` activates `ذ ك ر B007` (honorable mention and renown) and `ذ ك ر B009` (reminder), while fixed `كَفَرُوا` activates `ك ف ر B001` (covering) and `ك ف ر B003` (rejecting truth). The public utterance “mad” supplies the counter-reputation; I infer that the accusation is meant to cover both the reminder's standing and its bearer with an alternative public name. Rejection operates as reputational overlay, not silent disbelief.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 68:52 immediately strips the madness label of finality by restating the heard object as a reminder for all worlds. That later universal scope corrects the attempted reputational cover and preserves fixed `ٱلذِّكْر` as both admonition (`ذ ك ر B009`) and honorable public mention (`ذ ك ر B007`).

findings.text: Düşmanca bakış, pasif görme değil, kişinin toplumsal duruşunu kayganlaştırıp bulunduğu yerden sökmeye çalışan bir baskıdır.
Ses kulağa ulaştığı halde anlayış ve uyum doğurmaz; önceden taşınan delilik hükmü, duyulan öğüdün kavranmasını engeller.
Delilik suçlaması, öğüdün ve onu getirenin kamusal itibarını başka bir adla örtmeye çalışan bir ün saldırısıdır.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Protected Growth Turns Cover into Provision
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A productive enclosure protects living growth long enough for seed, plant, fruit, animal, and human occupant to reach a beneficial state.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Paradise is lexically materialized as shield, tree-cover, seed-cover, fruit husk, cultivated field, and usable tree product; protection is productive rather than merely defensive.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Seed-Cover and Fruit-Husk Guard Development
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Seed is covered in soil, new vegetation thickens, a fruit remains sheathed until ripe, and the yield emerges from its protected stage.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: covering seed with soil (`quranic:root_001307:B008/m01`); fruit or palm sheath (`quranic:root_001307:B010/m01`); dense plant growth (`quranic:root_000266:B011/m03`); ripe pasture or fruit ready for use (`quranic:root_000956:B007/m01`); young palms (`quranic:root_000248:B006/m01`); strong male plant (`quranic:root_000516:B002/m01`); crop yield and fruit (`quranic:root_000009:B007/m01`); persistent green growth (`quranic:root_000532:B012/m03`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Cover is stage-specific rather than absolute concealment. Soil and husk protect what is not ready; ripening and emerging yield then convert the covered potential into accessible provision.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Protected Growth Turns Cover into Provision

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Cultivation Produces Food, Fiber, Tannin, and Scent
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Fields are threshed and plowed; trees yield tanning material and aromatic substance that pass from ecology into craft and use.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: threshing grain underfoot (`quranic:root_000470:B005/m01`); long plow implements (`quranic:root_000741:B015/m01`); tanning tree and bark (`quranic:root_000737:B008/m01`); camphor as plant and perfume (`quranic:root_001307:B011/m01`); green tanning shrub (`quranic:root_000076:B005/m01`); gathered produce (`quranic:root_000009:B007/m02`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:35/43 `مُسْلِمِينَ`/`سَٰلِمُونَ` [س ل م]; 68:37 `تَدْرُسُ` [د ر س]; 68:41 `يَأْتُ` [ء ت ي]; 68:51 `سَمِعُ` [س م ع] and `كَفَرُ` [ك ف ر]; surface anchor unavailable for root `ء ل ي`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The garden’s yield extends beyond fruit. Threshing, plow, bark, tannin, and perfume show cultivation feeding both body and craft, while the unavailable `ء ل ي` anchor remains a purely lexical plant contribution.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Claims Become Durable Through Text, Judgment, and Guarantee
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A claim acquires force when it is assembled into a durable record, interpreted under judgment, and backed by a responsible party.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The polemical questions expose a complete documentary institution: material joining, written decree, study, scope, oath, guarantor, partner, fulfillment, and adjudication.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Question and Answer Expose the Missing Warrant
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: An interrogator requests a named basis; parties question one another, an answer affirms or refuses, and a putative explanation must identify its referent.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: request and inquiry (`quranic:root_000661:B001/m01`); thing requested (`quranic:root_000661:B002/m01`); reciprocal questioning (`quranic:root_000661:B004/m01`); attention-opening particle (`quranic:root_001573:B002/m01`); answer or response (`quranic:root_001573:B003/m01`); interrogative substitution (`quranic:root_001573:B004/m01`); interrogative-relative reference (`quranic:root_000527:B004/m02`); affirmative answer (`quranic:root_001525:B004/m01`); reported supposition (`quranic:root_001272:B011/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:40 `سَلْ` [س ء ل]; 68:51 `يَقُولُ` [ق و ل]; surface anchors unavailable for roots `ه ا ء` and `ذ و و`; 68:34 `نَّعِيمِ` [ن ع م].
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Interrogation is a warrant-seeking mechanism. It fixes the requested object, identifies who answers, and tests whether a demonstrable referent lies behind the assertion rather than leaving it as ungrounded supposition.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] The Body Must Be Able to Stand, Bend, and Obey
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Submission is a bodily capacity expressed through posture, jointed movement, lowered profile, and response to command.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Failure to prostrate is rendered as a breakdown across posture, limb, gaze, footing, tractability, and jointed capacity, not simply unwillingness at the final moment.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Low Ground, Spent Hump, and Hanging Edge Materialize Humbling
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A proud profile loses height like low ground, a setting star, or a depleted camel hump, while the body and garment hang downward.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: bowed humility (`quranic:root_000412:B001/m01`); low lifeless terrain (`quranic:root_000412:B002/m01`); sinking star (`quranic:root_000412:B003/m01`); hump with its crest depleted (`quranic:root_000412:B004/m01`); abasement under force (`quranic:root_000519:B001/m01`); gentle lowliness (`quranic:root_000519:B002/m01`); hanging lower edge (`quranic:root_000519:B005/m01`); struck peg (`quranic:root_000519:B006/m01`); head-and-chest lowering (`quranic:root_001307:B014/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Humbling is a loss of vertical prominence. Terrain, star, hump, garment edge, head, and chest all descend by different mechanisms, giving the verse’s lowered eyes and covering humiliation a coherent shape.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Perception Can Stabilize Knowledge or Strip Away Footing
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Sensory contact becomes reliable only when eye, ear, inward understanding, and stable bodily position cooperate.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Hostile looking is rendered as a literal destabilization of ground and skin, while hearing can progress to understanding or become weighted, bound, and merely reputational.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Sight Becomes Insight by Reading Marks
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: The eye registers a surface, inward sight interprets it, blood-trace or stone supplies visible evidence, and a remembered mark guides cognition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: ocular sight (`quranic:root_000121:B001/m02`); inward discernment (`quranic:root_000121:B002/m02`); visible blood trace (`quranic:root_000121:B004/m01`); pale gleaming stone (`quranic:root_000121:B007/m02`); knowledge as disclosure (`quranic:root_001040:B001/m03`); identifying landmark (`quranic:root_001040:B002/m02`); retained remembrance (`quranic:root_000516:B003/m01`); reminder restoring presence (`quranic:root_000516:B009/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Sight supplies data, not completion. Trace and landmark make the surface readable; remembrance preserves the evidence; inward discernment converts it into knowledge. This sequence contrasts with the hostile gaze that seeks effect without understanding.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Perception Can Stabilize Knowledge or Strip Away Footing
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Sensory contact becomes reliable only when eye, ear, inward understanding, and stable bodily position cooperate.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Hearing Moves from Ear to Comprehension or Burden
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Sound reaches the ear, is transmitted and understood, then either elicits compliance or is blocked by weight, binding, or ungrounded inference.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: auditory perception (`quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`); ear and auditory opening (`quranic:root_000741:B002/m01`); understanding and compliance (`quranic:root_000741:B003/m01`); making another hear (`quranic:root_000741:B004/m01`); auditory fetter (`quranic:root_000741:B009/m01`); inference from hearing and seeing without object (`quranic:root_000741:B013/m01`); brain as auditory center (`quranic:root_000741:B016/m01`); weighted unreceptive hearing (`quranic:root_000202:B009/m02`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Hearing is decomposed into organ, event, transmission, understanding, and response. A fettered or heavy ear may receive sound without accepting it, while hasty inference treats sensory contact as knowledge before an object has been secured.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: A Gaze Can Make Ground and Skin Slippery
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Hostile looking dislodges the target from a stable place as though the ground, animal body, or oiled skin had become too smooth to grip.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: slick barren surface that defeats footing (`quranic:root_000640:B001/m01`); slick animal hindquarter (`quranic:root_000640:B004/m01`); fast gliding camel (`quranic:root_000640:B006/m01`); oiled shining skin (`quranic:root_000640:B007/m01`); shaved smooth head (`quranic:root_000640:B008/m01`); hostile ocular act (`quranic:root_000121:B001/m03`); covering that blocks secure perception (`quranic:root_001307:B001/m01`).

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Madness Charge Confuses Hidden Mind with Covered Truth
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Observers encounter an inaccessible interior, cover the truth, and replace inquiry with an accusation that attributes corruption or derangement to the speaker.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: sensory concealment (`quranic:root_000266:B001/m03`); mind covered by madness (`quranic:root_000266:B006/m02`); hidden heart (`quranic:root_000266:B010/m02`); overpowering affliction (`quranic:root_000606:B001/m01`); attributed corruption and falsehood (`quranic:root_000606:B005/m01`); denial covering truth (`quranic:root_001307:B003/m01`); assigning unbelief to another (`quranic:root_001307:B006/m01`); false attribution in speech (`quranic:root_001272:B005/m02`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:43 `تَرْهَقُ` [ر ه ق]; 68:51 `كَفَرُ` [ك ف ر], `يَقُولُ` [ق و ل], and `مَجْنُونٌ` [ج ن ن].
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The accusation mistakes epistemic cover for diagnosed interior state. Concealment, denial, attribution, and overpowering affliction are different operations; their separation exposes how polemical naming substitutes for knowledge.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Utterance Summons, Attributes, and Makes Reputation
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Speech changes social reality by calling participants, asserting claims, circulating reports, and fixing a person’s public name.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The same communicative field includes prayer-call, council, riddle, public anecdote, praise, insult, false attribution, and truthful fulfillment; “speech” is split by operation and social effect.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: A Report Can Polish the Heart or Turn a Person into an Anecdote
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Renewed speech enters memory, circulates among hearers, and produces either inward clarification, durable renown, or public shame.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: renewed news or discourse (`quranic:root_000299:B003/m02`); becoming a public anecdote (`quranic:root_000299:B004/m01`); making a matter manifest (`quranic:root_000299:B006/m01`); polishing sword or heart (`quranic:root_000299:B007/m01`); verbal mention (`quranic:root_000516:B004/m01`); public honor and renown (`quranic:root_000516:B007/m01`); documentary memorial of a right (`quranic:root_000516:B008/m01`); reminder (`quranic:root_000516:B009/m02`); public repute (`quranic:root_000741:B005/m01`); insult made audible (`quranic:root_000741:B006/m01`); circulating report (`quranic:root_001272:B007/m04`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Public memory is made by transmission. A report can cleanse perception like polish, preserve a right in documentary mention, elevate a name, or turn that name into a cautionary anecdote or audible insult.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Utterance Summons, Attributes, and Makes Reputation
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Speech changes social reality by calling participants, asserting claims, circulating reports, and fixing a person’s public name.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The same communicative field includes prayer-call, council, riddle, public anecdote, praise, insult, false attribution, and truthful fulfillment; “speech” is split by operation and social effect.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: False Attribution Is Answered by Fulfilled Speech
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A doubtful assertion becomes explicit false attribution; counter-speech tests it against action, promise, and a stable definition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: assertion under suspicion (`quranic:root_000633:B001/m02`); vain expectation (`quranic:root_000633:B002/m01`); falsehood (`quranic:root_001290:B001/m02`); accusing another of falsehood (`quranic:root_001290:B002/m03`); failed charge or attack (`quranic:root_001290:B004/m01`); acting without delay (`quranic:root_001290:B005/m01`); false attribution (`quranic:root_001272:B005/m03`); imposed judgment (`quranic:root_001272:B010/m02`); formal definition (`quranic:root_001272:B016/m01`); truthful statement (`quranic:root_000852:B001/m02`); fulfilled promise (`quranic:root_000852:B004/m02`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The channel distinguishes saying, attributing, defining, and fulfilling. A claim is not vindicated by more forceful speech but by correspondence between the report, the named referent, and enacted promise.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Covering Establishes the Stakes of Disclosure and Exposure
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A cover creates an interior that may protect, hide, or entomb; lifting or losing it changes the occupant’s vulnerability and public status.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Unseen knowledge, armor, grave, grove, fruit-husk, uncovered defect, open hostility, exposed terrace, and abandoned child occupy distinct positions in one cover-removal mechanism.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Pit, Grove, Root, and Grave Make Nested Interiors
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A thing passes from ordinary visibility into a low place, dense growth, underground root, or grave, each providing a different depth and permanence of concealment.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: absence from eye and knowledge (`quranic:root_001117:B001/m01`); hidden pit or depression (`quranic:root_001117:B002/m01`); concealing grove (`quranic:root_001117:B003/m01`); hidden root later excavated (`quranic:root_001117:B008/m01`); burial (`quranic:root_001117:B009/m01`); sensory cover (`quranic:root_000266:B001/m04`); burial wrapping (`quranic:root_000266:B009/m02`); hiding-place (`quranic:root_000266:B017/m02`); vast darkness or water that covers (`quranic:root_001307:B002/m01`); fruit-sheath (`quranic:root_001307:B010/m02`); hidden mountain pass (`quranic:root_001307:B013/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:47 `غَيْبُ` [غ ي ب]; 68:51 `كَفَرُ` [ك ف ر] and `مَجْنُونٌ` [ج ن ن].
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Concealment has topology. Pit lowers, grove surrounds, root passes underground, grave seals, and mountain pass hides by terrain; this differentiates ordinary unseen knowledge from physical inaccessibility and burial.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Covering Establishes the Stakes of Disclosure and Exposure
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A cover creates an interior that may protect, hide, or entomb; lifting or losing it changes the occupant’s vulnerability and public status.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Unseen knowledge, armor, grave, grove, fruit-husk, uncovered defect, open hostility, exposed terrace, and abandoned child occupy distinct positions in one cover-removal mechanism.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Shield and Armor Preserve an Interior Under Attack
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A fitted shield, armor, or covering layer absorbs exterior force while keeping the enclosed body sound.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: protective barrier (`quranic:root_001677:B001/m02`); shield (`quranic:root_000266:B008/m04`); armor (`quranic:root_000121:B005/m03`); defensive weapon or mail (`quranic:root_000633:B005/m01`); covering layer (`quranic:root_001307:B001/m02`); wounded person named “sound” in hope or surrender (`quranic:root_000737:B009/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: This is protective concealment rather than epistemic evasion. The cover remains fitted to a vulnerable body and is judged by whether soundness survives the blow.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Extended time can be organized into incremental approach, deception, pursuit, and eventual arrival at a fixed limit.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Delay is not inactivity. Dictation, head-start, slow-kindling fire, stepwise luring, long pursuit, and final overtaking describe how time itself becomes an instrument.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Stepwise Luring Converts Movement into Entrapment
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A target advances one grade at a time, believing itself free, while stratagem and slow preparation carry it into an increasingly closed situation.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: walking a route (`quranic:root_000468:B001/m01`); incremental luring (`quranic:root_000468:B003/m01`); path toward extinction (`quranic:root_000468:B004/m01`); folding and insertion (`quranic:root_000468:B005/m01`); forceful manipulation (`quranic:root_001334:B001/m01`); stratagem and deceptive respite (`quranic:root_001334:B002/m01`); fire slow to kindle (`quranic:root_001334:B006/m01`); arduous seeking (`quranic:root_001329:B001/m01`); near-completion of an act (`quranic:root_001329:B002/m01`); luring an animal from its burrow (`quranic:root_000452:B006/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Gradation is the mechanism of deception. Each step remains locally plausible, yet fold, insertion, slow fire, and lure progressively reduce the target’s available exits.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Holding Pressure Can Preserve Control or Seal Distress Inside
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Restraint governs pressure by holding the self, closing an opening, tying parts, or building a structure able to bear load.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Patience and choking distress share a mechanics of containment, but differ in agency and outcome: one disciplines pressure; the other traps breath behind a sealed outlet.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Patience Holds the Self While Distress Holds the Breath
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A person restrains panic and anger, but under extreme pressure breath, speech, or life itself may become trapped within.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: self-restraint against panic (`quranic:root_000840:B001/m01`); coercive confinement (`quranic:root_000840:B002/m01`); no-exit adversity (`quranic:root_000840:B006/m01`); swallowed anger (`quranic:root_001303:B001/m01`); trapped breath and silence (`quranic:root_001303:B002/m01`); life struggling to leave (`quranic:root_001334:B003/m01`); inward unspoken statement (`quranic:root_001272:B012/m03`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:45 `كَيْدِ` [ك ي د]; 68:48 `ٱصْبِرْ` [ص ب ر], `نَادَىٰ` [ن د و], and `مَكْظُومٌ` [ك ظ م]; 68:51 `يَقُولُ` [ق و ل].
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Both patience and anguish hold something back, but patience retains governed agency while `مَكْظُوم` marks pressure trapped at the outlet. The contrast makes the command to endure a transformation of containment, not a demand for numbness.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Joined Parts Create Load-Bearing and Water-Handling Systems
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Cutting, joining, tying, and fitting convert separate materials into containers, conduits, rigging, and frames that can carry load or govern flow.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Stitched hide, tanning bark, sandal strap, bucket handle, well-rope splice, underground channel, body joint, shin, and tool-leg share an engineering logic of fitted parts under tension.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Rope, Handle, Basin, and Channel Complete a Water Circuit
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A rope is lengthened to reach water, attached to a handled bucket, raised over a well-edge, and emptied into a basin or managed conduit.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: well-rope splice and ring (`quranic:root_000471:B003/m01`); single-handled water-carrier's bucket (`quranic:root_000737:B011/m01`); bucket handle or balancing crosspiece (`quranic:root_000741:B008/m01`); linked wells or openings that preserve water flow (`quranic:root_001303:B005/m01`); binding loop that joins cord ends (`quranic:root_001303:B006/m01`); collected basin-water (`quranic:root_000220:B002/m01`); excavated rim around well or basin (`quranic:root_000220:B003/m01`); directed watercourse (`quranic:root_000009:B004/m01`); water-rich well or sea (`quranic:root_001040:B005/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Each component answers a different hydraulic problem: depth requires a splice, weight a handle, lifting a balanced attachment, collection a basin, and distribution a controlled channel. The scene is a complete flow system assembled from small lexical parts.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Ground Surface Controls Posture, Footing, and Exposure
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Surface composition and elevation determine whether a body can stand, lower itself, move securely, find cover, or remain publicly exposed.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Hard and soft stone, low dead earth, bare expanse, slick soil, hoof-protecting gait, mountain-center, hidden grove, floor cushion, and parapetless roof make bodily posture a property of terrain and shelter.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Low, Bare, or Slick Ground Changes the Body's Gait
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A body lowers itself toward lifeless ground, crosses an uncovered surface, or adjusts its gait when smoothness and roughness threaten secure footing.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: low lifeless terrain (`quranic:root_000412:B002/m01`); uncovered open ground (`quranic:root_001005:B004/m01`); slick barren surface that defeats footing (`quranic:root_000640:B001/m01`); animal guarding a sore hoof from rough ground (`quranic:root_001677:B003/m01`); walking and proceeding along a route (`quranic:root_000468:B001/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Posture responds to substrate. Lowness invites or figures lowering, exposure removes protective margins, slickness defeats traction, and painful roughness makes even a capable animal place each step defensively.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Ground Surface Controls Posture, Footing, and Exposure
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Surface composition and elevation determine whether a body can stand, lower itself, move securely, find cover, or remain publicly exposed.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Hard and soft stone, low dead earth, bare expanse, slick soil, hoof-protecting gait, mountain-center, hidden grove, floor cushion, and parapetless roof make bodily posture a property of terrain and shelter.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Shelter Distinguishes a Protected Interior from an Open Edge
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A person moves between grove, hiding-place, floor cushion, bare land, and an unguarded roof, each position supplying or removing a different kind of enclosure.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: roof without parapet (`quranic:root_000015:B003/m01`); hiding-place (`quranic:root_000266:B017/m01`); concealing grove (`quranic:root_001117:B003/m01`); cushion cast on the floor for sitting (`quranic:root_001466:B008/m01`); stripped body or land (`quranic:root_001005:B003/m01`); uncovered open ground (`quranic:root_001005:B004/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Cover is spatially graded. Grove and hiding-place obscure the occupant, a cushion supports an interior posture, the bare plain removes enclosure, and a roof without parapet raises the body while leaving its edge unprotected.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P3 68:34-52] Discourse Coordinates Endpoint, Location, and Reference
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Relational and deictic operators place an event at a limit, in a setting, or before an interlocutor, then identify or question the entity under discussion.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Endpoint, proximity, accompaniment, vague location, bounded day, demonstrative, relative, interrogative, attention-call, response, copular presence, and formal definition expose the small grammatical operations that stage a claim.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Pointing, Asking, Answering, and Defining Stabilize the Referent
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: An attention-call opens an exchange, a demonstrative or relative expression selects the referent, a question tests it, and an answer or formal definition closes ambiguity.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: relative “the one who” (`quranic:root_000527:B002/m01`); demonstrative pointer (`quranic:root_000527:B003/m01`); interrogative-relative “what?” (`quranic:root_000527:B004/m01`); attention-opening particle (`quranic:root_001573:B002/m01`); answer or response (`quranic:root_001573:B003/m01`); interrogative substitution (`quranic:root_001573:B004/m01`); request and inquiry (`quranic:root_000661:B001/m01`); formal definition (`quranic:root_001272:B016/m01`); occurrence made present in predication (`quranic:root_001332:B001/m02`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:40/46 `سَلْهُمْ`/`تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ` [س ء ل]; 68:41/43/48 forms of `ك و ن` [ك و ن]; 68:51 `يَقُولُ` [ق و ل]; surface anchors unavailable for roots `ذ و و` and `ه ا ء`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Reference is stabilized through an ordered exchange: summon attention, point or relate, interrogate, answer, and define. Copular presence then installs the selected entity inside a proposition rather than leaving it as an unattached name.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, istenen şeyi vermeme, belirli bir işi yapmama ve o işe önem verip yaklaşmama bildiren sabit olumsuz yapıları bir araya getirir. Dal bu yapılara bağlı bir ret alanı olarak korunabilir, ancak genel anlamda her türlü reddetmeye yayılmamalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnızca tanıklanan olumsuz kalıplara bağlıdır; genel engelleme, yoksun bırakma veya her tür isteksizlik anlamı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal bütünüyle belirli olumsuz kalıplara bağlıdır; bu kalıplardaki vermeme, yapmama ve yanaşmama anlamları yalın köke genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Belirli olumsuz kalıplarla, istenen şeyi vermeyi veya sözü edilen işi yapmayı kesin biçimde reddetmektir. Bir kalıp ayrıca işe önem vermeyi ve onu yapmaya yaklaşmayı birlikte olumsuzlar.

facets.statement: Sabit bir olumsuz yapı, verme veya yapma yönündeki kesin isteksizliği bildirir.
Bir isteğe cevap olarak, istenen şeyi talep edene vermeme bildirilir.
Bir başka kalıp, belirli bir işi önemsememeyi ve onu yapmaya hiç yaklaşmamayı birlikte bildirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu tanıklık, olumsuz kalıpların vermeyi veya yapmayı reddettiğini; bir kalıbın ayrıca işe önem verme ve yaklaşma ihtimalini de dışladığını gösterir.

concept_gloss.text: vermeyi ya da yapmayı kesin biçimde reddetmek
concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnızca tanıklanan olumsuz kalıpların bir talebi geri çevirme veya bir işi yapmaya hiç yanaşmama işlevini topluca açıklamak için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Olumsuz kalıba bağlı kesin reddi ve verme ya da yapma kapsamını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir talepte bulunan kişiye istediği şeyi vermenin kesin biçimde reddedildiği bağlamlar içindir.

error_profile.preserves: Talep edilen şeyi vermeme ve bunu kesin bir ret olarak bildirme anlamını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Belirli bir işi önemseme, isteme ve gerçekleştirmeye yaklaşma ihtimallerinin birlikte dışlandığı bağlamlar içindir.

error_profile.preserves: İşi yapmama ve onu yapmaya yaklaşmayı reddetme anlamını korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: Bunu ne önemsiyorum ne de yapmaya yanaşıyorum.

error_profile.collision: Genel önleme ve alıkoyma dallarıyla karışır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi belirli yapılarda bir kişiden istenen şeyi ve konuşanın bir eylemi yapma isteğini bildirir. Bununla birlikte eylem isteği yorumu belirli bir söz için bazı yorumculara bağlandığından, bütün yakın-eylem kullanımlarına yayılan genel bir anlam gibi sunulmamalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal belirli yapılardaki istek ve niyet anlamıyla sınırlıdır; eyleme yaklaşma veya eylemi gerçekten başlatma anlamına gelmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam farklı fakat belirli yapılarda tanıklanır; bir kişiden bekleneni bildiren kullanım ile yoruma bağlı niyet kullanımı ayrılır ve yalın köke genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Belirli yapılarda bir kişiden istenen şeyi veya konuşanın bir eylemi yapma niyetini bildirir. İkinci kullanım, kaynakta belirli bir söz için aktarılmış sınırlı bir yorumdur.

facets.statement: Bir kişiden istenen ya da beklenen şey bildirilebilir.
Belirli bir sözde, konuşanın bir eylemi yapmayı istemesi biçiminde yorumlanan kullanım vardır.
Çekimli biçimlerin istek ve niyet alanına ait olduğu ayrıca açıkça belirtilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Dal, belirli yapılarda istenen şeyi bildirir; aynı tanıklık, bir sözdeki kullanımın niyet anlamıyla yorumlandığını ve çekimli biçimlerin istek alanında değerlendirildiğini aktarır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, anlamı bir şeyi yoğun çaba göstererek ele alma, onunla uğraşma ve onu işleme olarak kurar. Bu çekirdek anlam aldatma, savaş veya başka özel kullanımlarla sınırlandırılmamıştır.
